prompt: is eignevector a basis for the eigenspace
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 directly answers the question by stating the correct condition: an eigenvector spans (and thus can form a basis of) the eigenspace only when the eigenspace is 1-dimensional. Candidate 4 is more tangential but still relevant, giving a method to test whether vectors form a basis of an eigenspace and includes a correct worked example; however it omits the key dimension/eigenspace-spanning condition and only implicitly connects to the “single eigenvector” case. Candidates 2 and 3 largely avoid the actual “eigenvector vs. eigenspace basis” condition and make overgeneral/incorrect claims about eigenvectors forming a basis for the whole vector space without the necessary prerequisites.
